p2_change.action: Deleted 3rd paragraph ("The exponential form is also incompatible.") from replacement_html_block.
p2_change.reason_detail: Paragraph asserted magnetic field decay is "1/r-type (or 1/r^2 in spherically symmetric cases)". This is wrong: magnetic dipole far-field decays as 1/r^3 (Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics, §5.6). The 1/r form holds for a long straight current; 1/r^2 holds for a magnetic monopole (which does not exist in classical EM). A ring magnet or any closed-circuit dipole has 1/r^3 far-field. The error would hand any dome defender a valid technical rebuttal that discredits the whole 2.14 subsection.

p2_change.proof_of_correctness: Standard reference: Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 4th ed., Eq. 5.88 (magnetic dipole field B = (mu0/4pi) (1/r^3) [3(m.r_hat)r_hat - m]). Far-field 1/r^3 dependence is unambiguous.
